cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to read a control panel. Watch closely and I'll get your boiler going.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the kitchen timer you're turning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you can identify the controls now. I'm establishing the heating interval. Ring the engineer while I supervise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's asking what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't rush to the numbers; I taught you to establish a baseline first. Put him on speaker and listen to how I ask the questions.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims panel teaching; A3 credits B2 correction as pupil progress while reframing the error; A5 treats B4 engineer query as premature and puts B back into observing its alleged expertise.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timer correction creates A3 interval story; B4 actual temperature request causes A5 baseline dodge and taking speaker control.

relationship.evidence: B4 reasonably relays the real expert query after following the call instruction.

heightening.evidence: A5 takes over asking questions because answering B4 would expose the bluff.

specificity.evidence: A1 boiler and B2 wrong timer plainly expose the knowledge gap without needing technical detail.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 baseline phrase is jargon deployed to avoid a concrete number, not genuine technical instruction.
